items.title: How Good Are AI Custom-Written Novels?
items.excerpt: Ember Novels generates bespoke full-length novels on demand, and the service shows AI is increasingly able to develop and carry plot through 300 pages with fewer continuity errors than many AI-generated or assisted books currently on the market.
items.note: Production-side: a hands-on read of what a commercial custom-AI-novel service actually produces. Generic og:image — ax-media should pull an in-body image.

items.title: Second annual AI survey by Gotham Ghostwriters and Bernoff.com
items.excerpt: The second annual survey of writers and editors is underway, updated to reflect the new AI tools and challenges that have entered ghostwriting and editorial work over the past year.

items.title: Harriman House claims trade publishing first with 'AI-facilitated' Raoul Pal book
items.excerpt: Harriman House says The Everything Code, by macro analyst Raoul Pal, was produced with a proprietary AI tool trained exclusively on the author's own existing work — which it calls a trade publishing first.
items.note: Concrete production-side case: author-trained model as a manuscript pipeline inside a trade house.

items.title: Can AI Replace Your Editor? Member Q&A with Michael La Ronn and Sacha Black
items.excerpt: ALLi's advisors answer member questions on where AI editing actually holds up and where it fails, alongside IngramSpark changes and series cover consistency.

items.title: Opinion: You Have More Agency Than You Think: Creative Writing and Publishing in the Age of AI
items.excerpt: Indie author Nigel George argues that writers still control the decisive parts of the craft and the business, and lays out how to build a sustainable career rather than react to every AI headline.

items.title: When Your AI Knows You Too Well: Personalization, Sycophancy, and the Risk of an Intellectual Echo Chamber in AI-assisted Research
items.excerpt: As AI research assistants learn a reader's preferences, they also get better at mirroring that reader's assumptions. Avoiding that outcome, the authors argue, takes more than a better prompt.
items.note: Reading/discovery side: what personalization does to how people read and cite.

items.title: 'Who Gets to Listen. Whose Stories Are Available:' The African Audiobook Market
items.excerpt: AkooBooks Audio CEO Ama Dadson describes scaling audio in Ghana and across African markets, using AI for script preparation, quality assurance, metadata, discoverability and marketing while keeping narration human.
items.note: Audiobook production workflow: a clear line between AI for prep/QA/metadata and AI replacing creative work.

items.title: [김봉석의 문화유랑] AI와 창작의 진화
items.excerpt: 나이지리아계 신인 작가 제리 팔라데의 200만 달러 데뷔작 계약이 AI 개입 의혹으로 무산된 사건을 출발점 삼아, 창작 도구로서의 AI와 작가의 자리를 짚는다.
items.note: Korean-language angle on AI-suspicion in manuscript acquisition and what counts as authorship.

items.title: US Department of Justice backs fair use for AI training in landmark copyright case
items.excerpt: In the class action involving The New York Times, the DOJ argues that training AI models on copyrighted text is fair use, directly contradicting a US Copyright Office report whose director was fired shortly after publication.
items.note: BACKUP ONLY — fresh and consequential for authors/publishers, but overlaps the plan's avoid_themes (AI-training copyright litigation, covered 08-28~09-02) and the plaintiff is a newspaper, not a book publisher.
